subject: reworking ordinal regression & pos_ordered data type

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: reworking ordinal regression & pos_ordered data type
parts:
Major change alert.

Andrew changed his mind from ARM on how to
parameterize ordinal logistic regression, so I'm
going to change Stan to follow.

In ARM, there were (K-2) positive, ordered cutpoints,
with the 0 treated implicitly as the first cutpoint.
That's why there is a "pos_ordered" data type and
why the ordered_logistic() distribution wanted (K-2)
positive cut points for a K-way ordinal regression.
(This was for identifiability in regressions with
an intercept.)

I'm going to:

1. Remove the "pos_ordered" data type.

2. Add an "ordered" data type that takes real values
in increasing order in a column vector.

3. Change the parameterization of ordinal_logistic_log()
to take (K-1) ordered (but not nec. positive) cut points.

4. Rewrite all unit tests for the data type and the
distribution.

5. Rewrite the manual sections on pos_ordered data types,
and add warnings about non-identifiability.

That'll keep me busy for a couple of days.

After that, I'm back to writing the rest of the manual
programming techniques sections.

- Bob

messages.author: 417414441a0ca1d9
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] reworking ordinal regression & pos_ordered data type
parts:
Since you're thinking about logistics, does Stan handle multinomial
logistic regression, i.e., non-ordinal but with more than 2 outcomes?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] reworking ordinal regression & pos_ordered data type
parts:
We can do multi-logit pretty directly as:

y[n] ~ categorical(softmax(x[n] * beta));

where beta is the (K x D) coefficient vector
and x[n] the (D x 1) row vector of predictors.

This makes me realize I should add a chapter
to the manual on how to code regressions.

We'll eventually add:

y[n] ~ categorical_softmax(x[n] * beta);

One advantage is that we can unfold the gradient
calcs a few steps to save time and memory.

Another question is whether we'd also want to
directly parameterize in terms of the regression
coefficients:

y[n] ~ multi_logit_regression(x[n],beta);

This is even better for unfolding the derivatives

The only thing stopping us is the time taken to
code the function and error checking and to code the
unit testing and write the doc.

- Bob
